purpose: Confirm or reject the proposed 24-byte digit-vector reconstruction cost behind the repeated 12024-byte signed-word construction excess.
trigger: Both closed combined and cache-free trials report unchanged 12501 allocation calls, 652000 to 664024 requested bytes, unchanged 388000 retained bytes and peak 388264 to 388288 for the original 1000-input signed-word construction phase.
libraries: Reuse the original main release hyperreal, serde_json and num libraries. The Rational constructor source must be byte-identical in all three prior variants. No library rebuild or runtime source change.
inputs: Extract all 19 integer literals directly from the original three-family integer probe. Check all available direct clone/primitive magnitude and original/signed-word Rational constructor paths. Replay the original six signed-word values cyclically for 1000 conversions; 501 fit i64.
measurement: System requested-allocation histograms, total calls/bytes, retained and peak deltas. Fixed atomic storage; collect/format only after stopping counters. Single-threaded standalone process, no spawned work. Canonical constants are warmed equally outside all observations.
controls: Empty scope, one 17-byte zeroed allocation with matching retained/histogram, and disabling on unwind. All case values independently match parsed exact Rational/BigInt magnitudes.
rows: 71 case/method rows, two 1000-conversion batches and one allocator control in each process. Raw rows retained whether the allocation mechanism matches the hypothesis or not.
analysis: Verify every row/histogram, original input literals, reversed order and unchanged evidence. Compare both process counts and the whole 1000-conversion excess without collecting timings. Allocation-mechanism confirmation is scoped to this backend and these direct constructors.
limits: This probe omits the surrounding affine fixture; it cannot replace the original costs.
No direct causal claim about the separate quadratic construction timings or any native deadline.
A proposed borrowed-integer helper remains unimplemented and unadmitted until correctness and the existing end-to-end costs are checked.
